identity.real_world_identity_notes: The Alpine A424 is an LMDh prototype using the category's common Xtrac P1359 hybrid transmission. The base AMS2 telemetry identity was live-tested. The exact Low Downforce identity is treated as an aero-package alias inheriting the base controls and has not been separately live-tested.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct AMS2 cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim with an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, AMS2 1.6.9.91 moved the car from rest without physical clutch input. The common LMDh hybrid architecture supports interpreting this as electric launch behavior rather than a generic driving aid.
Seven forward gears were selected by paddles while holding full throttle, without clutch input or throttle lift. Every upshift was accepted.

No upshift power interruption was perceptible. Automatic cut is therefore medium-confidence, supported by the common LMDh transmission, successful full-throttle shifts, and the three shift-cut-positive LMDh peers in the 1.5.5.2 source.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted with the driver's foot fully off the throttle. Automatic blip was directly visible as a throttle-display spike.

The exact Alpine A424 - Low Downforce telemetry identity is approved as an aero-package alias inheriting these controls. Only the base identity was live-tested; the Low Downforce configuration remains an explicit assumption to revisit if contrary behavior is observed.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Hybrid move-off, seven paddle-selected forward gears, no-lift clutch-free upshifts, clutch-free downshifts, and a visible automatic throttle blip were observed directly.
Automatic cut remains medium-confidence because no discrete power interruption was perceptible during full-throttle shifts.
Base controls were live-tested; the exact Low Downforce identity inherits them as an approved aero-package assumption.

confidence.basis: Identity and most control behavior were directly observed and hardware is supported by primary sources; automatic cut is a medium-confidence class and behavior inference rather than a measured interruption.

claims.basis: Official release listing plus exact live CarModel, CarId, and LMDh CarClass values observed through SimHub 9.11.22.

The Low Downforce name is an exact observed SimHub identity. Its controls are explicitly inherited from the live-tested base car because the variant is understood to be an aero package; the variant itself has not been live-tested.
Alpine identifies the Xtrac gearbox, Xtrac specifies seven-speed sequential pneumatic actuation, and all seven paddle-selected forward gears were exercised in AMS2.
The clutch-free move-off was directly observed with Auto Clutch disabled; primary LMDh sources establish the integrated MGU and electric-only low-speed movement that explain the behavior.

Seven clutch-free full-throttle upshifts establish that no lift is required. Automatic cut is inferred from the common LMDh gearbox and the three shift-cut-positive LMDh peers in the older source because no interruption was perceptible in this test.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted with no driver throttle input, and the automatic blip was directly visible as a throttle-display spike.
Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim with an integrated display.

notes: Simulator-specific behavior is kept distinct from the real LMDh hardware evidence, especially for automatic shift cut.
Low Downforce is an exact approved alias whose controls are inherited from the verified base car; it has not been separately live-tested.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "prototype", a value that named a racing category rather than a rim outline. That value is retired: the rims it covered are the same closed form, flattened at both the top and the bottom, that the project now records as "gt-style". The shape was remapped by definition and the rim was not observed again.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
